expected_tables.notes: Table 1: maximum path length / per-layer complexity / sequential operations comparison across layer types (Self-Attention, Recurrent, Convolutional, Self-Attention restricted).
Table 2: BLEU scores and training cost comparison; has a grouped/merged header spanning BLEU and Training Cost (FLOPs) column groups.
Table 3: architecture variations grid (rows A-E), wide table with many numeric columns, likely to wrap or split visually in a PDF-to-text pass.
Table 4: English constituency parsing F1 comparison.

math_notes: Heavy LaTeX-rendered math throughout section 3 (scaled dot-product attention formula, multi-head attention concat/projection formulas, positional encoding sinusoidal formulas in 3.5). Equations are embedded as inline PDF vector/glyph typesetting, not MathML or images, so any math-detection heuristic will only see them via raw glyph extraction (pdftotext renders them as garbled Unicode math-alphanumeric symbol runs, e.g. broken fraction bars and stacked subscripts) — a good stress test for whether math-detection is confused by numbered section headings that follow a similarly numeric pattern (e.g. is '3.2' a heading or part of an equation reference).

notes_for_implementer: This is a clean, well-formed LaTeX two-column academic PDF: headings are NOT tagged in any structural/semantic sense at the PDF level (PDF has no native heading concept) but ARE fully numbered and stylistically consistent (larger/bold font), so a font-size-and-numbering heuristic should succeed here. This fixture is a 'should mostly just work' native-PDF baseline for comparison against the scanned/exported PDF fixtures (03, 04, 16, 17, 18). Two-column layout means naive left-to-right, top-to-bottom text extraction (without column awareness) will interleave the two columns' text incorrectly mid-paragraph -- pdftotext -layout handles this reasonably but a naive extractor may not.
